title: Choose Parche's new visual world
question: The roll assigned Chiva Route Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Chiva Route Board
options.lineage: Colombian chiva buses: painted stripe bands and the hand-lettered list of towns on the side
options.thesis: Your trip is the route painted on the side of the bus: each city you add is lettered onto the board.
options.viewport: Phone: stripe-band header with the trip name, the route board below listing stops as lettered rows with a search field and a visible city list under it, one big 'Add stop' action.
options.risk: Turns folkloric costume if stripes go everywhere; stripes stay on the route board and the header only.

raised.raise: Each step shows only the next decision: the city list answers 'where next?' and nothing else competes.
Every crew member owns one stripe colour, reused on their name, avatar and their share of the budget.
Stops carry strict sequence numbers (1, 2, 3) that every screen reuses.
A date clash renders structurally (crossed stripes on the clashing stops), not only as red text.

options.label: Metro Line Diagram
options.lineage: Metro de Medellín / TransMilenio line maps
options.thesis: The route is a transit line: each city is a station, and the line draws itself as you add stops.
options.viewport: Phone: vertical line with station dots down the left, city names beside them, an open station slot at the end with the city search and its list.
options.risk: The most predictable answer for a route builder; clean but could feel like any transit app.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Signs
options.thesis: Every screen is a junction sign: one yellow band says what you can do next.
options.viewport: Phone: a sticky yellow band 'Where are you starting?', monumental code of the chosen city, the city list as sign rows with arrows.
options.case: Wins clarity (each screen names the next move); weaker on identity, airports read generic for a friends' bus-and-plane trip.
options.risk: Reads like an airline app; yellow everywhere tires fast.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Crew as a roster of characters.
options.case: Loses both axes: trips are not characters.
options.kept: One fixed colour per person, reused everywhere.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything as a numbered catalog entry.
options.case: Loses both: coded labels hide what to do.
options.kept: Strict sequence numbers on every stop.

options.label: Exposure Zone Sheets
options.case: Loses both: no tie to friends travelling.
options.kept: Conflicts drawn as structure, not just colour.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Cities as stars, route as constellation.
options.case: Loses both: pretty, but no one reads a trip as a sky.
options.kept: Dot size as hierarchy: nights stayed set each stop's weight.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Loses both: no link to the trip or the crew.
options.kept: One display form repeated on a strict size ladder.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Wanderlog-style planner: white cards, a map, blue accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Phone: map strip on top, search field, list of added cities as cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every travel planner by design.
